description: Master programming by recreating your favorite technologies from scratch.

sources.entry: build-your-own-x: compilation of well-written, step-by-step guides for re-creating our favorite technologies from scratch

summary.one_liner: A curated list of step-by-step tutorials for re-creating popular technologies (compilers, databases, shells, browsers, operating systems, and more) from scratch in many programming languages.
summary.what_it_does: This is an awesome-style link collection rather than a software project. The README groups links by technology under headings such as "Build your own Database", "Build your own Shell", and "Build your own Operating System". Under each heading, entries are listed with the implementation language in bold and a link title, and some are marked [video] or [pdf]. Categories cover roughly 30 areas, from 3D renderers and blockchains to Git, Docker, neural networks, and web servers. An "Uncategorized" section collects tutorials that do not fit elsewhere. The README says contributions are welcome by pull request or issue.
use_cases: find a tutorial for building a programming language or compiler
learn how Git or Docker works by reimplementing it
follow a guide to write a shell or text editor
study operating system development step by step
pick a project to learn a language by building something
find tutorials for building a database or web server
notable: Organized by technology, with each entry tagged by implementation language
Covers many areas, including compilers, operating systems, databases, emulators, and neural networks
Marks video and PDF resources in the link text
Maintained by CodeCrafters, Inc. and open to pull requests
caveats: Links point to external sites, so availability and quality vary by entry
Many listed tutorials are in languages other than the one you may want
Entries are not ranked or reviewed beyond community submissions
